newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.4 pct to two-month-high.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.4 pct to two-month-high.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt an average 2.4 percent on Tuesday in strong selective activity to pierce major resistance at the index's 70,000 level, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed at 70,846.76, up 1,660.04 points from Monday. It had eased 0.44 percent on Monday after failing to overcome the 70,000 barrier following last week's 7.3 percent surge.
The previous highest close was 71,195.00 on July 12.

"The index may rise towards 72,000 now that it has pierced 70,000. It looks as though strong activity will continue although a necessary down correction did not occure at 70,000. There was limited cash entry," said Atilla Sozudogru from Bab securities.
Brokers said the market focused on shares of largely state-owned firms which are highly capitalised and thus have significant impact on the market index.
Nine-month profit expectations in companies also fuelled purchases in other stocks, they added.
A medium-term uptrend was said to have started last week amid cash influx and market optimism.
Trade volume increased to 12.4 trillion lira from Monday's 12.14 trillion.

The 85-share industrial index .ISEI gained 2.39 percent to 77,754.54 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF leapt 2.41 percent to 62,687.72. Of the 225 issues traded, gainers sharply outdid losers by 138 to 37 and 50 closed stable.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 200 lira at 10,200, Turkish Airlines, up 500 lira at 30,500, Akin Tekstil, up 500 lira at 10,250 and utility Aktas Elektrik, down 2,000 lira at 52,000. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 0875
